## Recommendation
- **Go to St. Joseph by boat. I'd rate it 3 of 4 (good).** Run small crankbaits or spoons at 20-30 ft for coho and 50-60 ft for Chinook.
- **South Haven is a close second, also about 3.** Fish 45-60 ft with small crankbaits and spoons, and try spawn on the bottom.
- **Grand Haven and Muskegon are about 1 of 4 (below average).** Their latest boat reports were mixed or thin, so I'd only go there with a specific reason.

## Why
- **St. Joseph has the strongest boat report:** the Apr 30 St. Joseph report rated boat coho and Chinook both good, with fish in 20-30 ft and 50-60 ft (St. Joseph, 2025-04-30).
- **South Haven's boat fishing was also good, but the water dropped sharply:** the buoy showed a 7 F drop over the latest week, which can signal upwelling (South Haven, 2025-04-30; buoy summary).
- **Grand Haven and Muskegon were weaker:** the latest Muskegon boat report called fishing "hit or miss" (quality 1), and Grand Haven's latest boat report was only a few coho and brown trout near shore (Muskegon, 2025-04-30; Grand Haven, 2025-04-23).
- **Past seasons at similar water temperature were mixed:** I'd expect boat fishing to vary a lot week to week this time of year.

## Evidence
**Recent reports** (newest report is 2025-04-30, six days old)
- St. Joseph (2025-04-30): "Salmon fishing continued to be very good as boat anglers made good catches of coho salmon." Small crankbaits trolled in 20-30 ft worked best. Chinook were caught in 50-60 ft (quality 3 for both).
- South Haven (2025-04-30): "Boat anglers had good fishing, with 45 to 60 feet of water being the most productive." Small crankbaits and spoons caught most fish, and spawn on the bottom worked well (quality 3, mixed coho and Chinook).
- Muskegon (2025-04-30): "Fishing was still hit or miss for boat anglers who were trolling but those that found the fish had success" (quality 1).
- Grand Haven (2025-04-23): boat anglers near shore caught "a few brown trout and coho salmon" (quality 1). No newer Grand Haven boat report exists in the database.

**Past seasons** (similar surface water, about 48 F; history, not current)
- Boat results ranged from good to slow. For example, St. Joseph in 2022 and 2023 had good boat fishing at 30 ft and 80 ft, while St. Joseph in 2024 had only a few coho at 30 ft (quality 1).
- After sharp drops, results were mixed. South Haven in May 2022 (a 7 F drop) had slow boat fishing (quality 1), while South Haven in May 2023 (a 6 F drop) had good boat fishing (quality 3).

**Conditions now** (the tool returned a summary for the week before May 6, not live data)
- Buoy surface water: St. Joseph 50 F (down 2 F), South Haven 47 F (down 7 F), Grand Haven 45 F (up 2 F), Muskegon 45 F (up 2 F).
- No wind forecast was returned, so I can't judge wind or wave conditions for this week.

## Caveats
- The newest boat reports are from April 23 to April 30, so the ratings are a guide, not a confirmed read on this week.
- The buoy temperatures are measured but come from a summary of the prior week, and the tool did not return a live update or a modeled pierhead temperature.
- The South Haven 7 F drop could mean upwelling and better fish, or a shift that slows the bite. Check the water again before you leave.
- Grand Haven has no recent boat-specific detail beyond a few incidental catches, so its rating is the least certain.
- Check the wind before you go. No forecast was available, and the 20+ mph wind guideline for small boats applies.

- Grand Haven, South Haven, St. Joseph, Muskegon DNR bulletin, week of Apr 23, 2025: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3dd426e
